quickStart.item_27: If anyone is in immediate danger or has a life-threatening emergency, call 999 or 112. Give the operator the exact location and postcode.
quickStart.item_25: For urgent medical advice that is not a life-threatening emergency, use NHS 111 or the relevant NHS service for the nation; service routes differ across Great Britain.
quickStart.item_47: Locate the exported ZIP and extract it to a private, secure folder. Keep an untouched copy of the original export.
quickStart.item_64: Start with emergency contacts, health information, legal document locations, insurance, bank accounts, pensions, and essential bills.
quickStart.item_03: Do not use another person's bank cards, online banking, passwords, or devices without the proper authority. Contact the relevant provider and follow its bereavement process.
quickStart.item_63: Share the pack only with trusted people who need it. Keep passwords, PINs, one-time codes, and recovery keys out of the exported files.

legalNotes.item_123: This guide is general information, not legal, tax, insurance, or financial advice. Rules depend on the facts and the relevant UK jurisdiction.
legalNotes.item_28: Great Britain means England, Scotland, and Wales; Northern Ireland is not covered by this GB configuration and has separate processes.
legalNotes.item_103: Probate in England and Wales and confirmation in Scotland are not interchangeable. Scotland has distinct succession, estate, and power-of-attorney rules; obtain advice for the relevant jurisdiction.
legalNotes.item_37: In England, Scotland, and Wales, GOV.UK says Tell Us Once may be available after registration or qualifying coroner certification. Northern Ireland and people permanently living abroad are excluded; check current eligibility and use any reference within its stated validity period.
legalNotes.item_115: Tell Us Once does not notify every private organisation. Banks, mortgage providers, insurers, employers, and many personal or workplace pension schemes may still need to be contacted directly.
legalNotes.item_17: Do not distribute an estate, assume a particular account passes automatically, or pay another person's debts without confirming authority, ownership, and applicable law.
legalNotes.item_76: Official guidance: What to do when someone dies: https://www.gov.uk/when-someone-dies
legalNotes.item_64: Official guidance: Applying for probate in England and Wales: https://www.gov.uk/applying-for-probate
legalNotes.item_67: Official guidance: Making a will: https://www.gov.uk/make-will
legalNotes.item_68: Official guidance: Managing a lasting power of attorney: https://www.gov.uk/manage-lasting-power-attorney

recoveryRoadmap.description: A general checklist for family representatives after a death. The correct legal and tax process depends on whether the relevant jurisdiction is England, Wales, or Scotland.

meta.title: Family Recovery Roadmap - Great Britain
meta.reviewedBy: Official guidance reviewed; not a substitute for legal or tax advice

intro.condolence: We are sorry for your loss. This checklist is intended to help organise the first practical steps.
intro.howToUse: Confirm the jurisdiction and your authority first. Then secure records, notify the right organisations, and obtain professional advice where needed.

startHere.0: If there is an immediate safety or medical emergency, call 999 or 112.
startHere.1: Register the death and follow the registrar or coroner's instructions; timing and process differ between Scotland and England or Wales.
startHere.2: Ask the registrar whether Tell Us Once is available and obtain its reference if applicable. It does not notify all private providers.
startHere.3: Locate the will, identify the executor or appropriate representative, and confirm the correct jurisdiction before acting.
startHere.4: Secure identity, property, bank, insurance, pension, debt, and tax records. Keep a log of every organisation contacted.
startHere.5: Do not access accounts, distribute assets, or pay debts until authority and provider requirements have been checked.

legalFramework.0: England and Wales: probate and estate administration processes; see GOV.UK applying for probate.
legalFramework.1: Scotland: confirmation and Scottish estate administration processes; see the Scottish Courts and Tribunals Service.
legalFramework.2: Wills, succession, powers of attorney, tax, benefits, and property rules can differ by jurisdiction and individual circumstances.
legalFramework.3: Tell Us Once can notify specified government departments in England, Scotland, and Wales when eligibility requirements are met; private organisations may need separate notification.
legalFramework.4: Official guidance may change. Confirm all forms, eligibility, fees, and deadlines with the relevant authority or a qualified adviser.

2.why: This protects property and helps representatives find the information needed for later steps.

2.title: Estate, tax, and property administration
2.focus: Confirm the required authority, value the estate, and complete the appropriate tax and property processes.

2.action: Keep complete records of decisions, valuations, expenses, provider correspondence, and distributions.
2.why: Representatives may need to account to beneficiaries, creditors, HMRC, or a court.

3.action: Check title, mortgage, insurance, and occupancy arrangements before selling, transferring, or changing property.
3.why: Title, co-ownership, lender, and jurisdiction rules can affect what can be done and when.

deathRegistration.action: Follow the registrar or coroner's instructions. Published registration timeframes differ between Scotland and England or Wales and may be affected by the circumstances.

tellUsOnce.scope: May be used for eligible deaths of people living in England, Scotland, or Wales; not for a person living in Northern Ireland or permanently abroad.
tellUsOnce.importantNote: It notifies specified public bodies, not every private organisation.

estateAuthority.englandAndWales: Check whether a grant of probate or letters of administration are required.
estateAuthority.scotland: Check the Scottish confirmation and estate administration process.

pensionTracing.service: The Pension Tracing Service can find contact details for a pension scheme; it cannot confirm whether a pension exists or its value.

0.definition: A person named in a will who may apply to deal with the estate, subject to the applicable jurisdiction and legal process.

1.definition: An England and Wales legal document that can authorise an executor to deal with an estate; whether it is needed depends on the circumstances and institutions involved.

2.definition: The Scottish court authority used by an executor to administer a deceased person's estate, where required.

3.definition: An England and Wales legal arrangement. Scotland has separate continuing and welfare power-of-attorney arrangements.

4.definition: A service for eligible people living in England, Scotland, or Wales to report a death to specified government organisations.
